texts: good. the salt-bloomed restriction becomes the condition of a rule that fires, and surviving cold-threshold nights is covered with nothing added.

mixed: the lantern side is right and the rule fires, but "on cold-threshold nights" is dropped into the time slot as a bare kind label - a slot that only holds dates, named times and parts of the day - so the every-such-night recurrence your plural carries is silently lost. Give the night a clause of its own: "When a cold-threshold night comes, unprepared lanterns on the Cliff Path die." The "when" clause makes each such night an occasion the dying can be tied to, so the every-time reading is stated rather than assumed, and spelling out "on the Cliff Path" records that location instead of the vaguer association a bare premodifier gets.
